reading.title: Five Ways to Tell a True Story
reading.purpose: Compare the different nonfiction forms writers use to share real memories and human lives.
paras: Not every true story has the same shape. Writers pick a form based on how much time they want to cover. They also decide whether to write about themselves or about someone else.

When a writer tells the tale of her whole life from childhood to now, the book is an autobiography. A memoir is narrower: it focuses on memories from one specific season or theme, such as a single summer spent learning to sail. Both forms shine in a reflective voice, where the author pauses to think deeply about what those days meant.

Shorter pieces zoom in even closer. An anecdote is a brief true story told to make a point, like a coach sharing a funny practice slip to teach teamwork. A vignette goes smaller still. It paints a sharp picture of one quiet moment—like warm bread in a kitchen—without needing a long plot.

Sometimes the most vital writer is an eyewitness, a person who saw a big event with his own eyes. Reporters prize firsthand notes because someone on the scene can recount the exact steps of what happened, detail by detail, instead of repeating loose rumors.

True stories can also shine a light on other people. A short profile sketches a real person's daily work and spirit. A tribute honors someone to show lasting thanks or care. Whatever the length, true-life writing saves moments that might fade away.

choices: a full-length book covering an author's entire life from birth
a short sketch that paints a vivid picture of one small moment
a newspaper report gathered from three separate rumors
a speech honoring a neighbor for decades of volunteer work
qs.why: Paragraph 3 describes a vignette as "painting a vivid picture of one quiet moment" without needing a long plot.

qs.q: Which sentence explains how a memoir differs from an autobiography?
choices: Not every true story has the same shape.
A memoir is narrower: it focuses on memories from one specific season or theme, such as a single summer spent learning to sail.
Shorter pieces zoom in even closer.
Whatever the length, true-life writing preserves moments that might otherwise fade.
qs.why: This sentence directly contrasts a memoir's focus on one season or theme with an autobiography's coverage of a whole life.

ev.text: A memoir is narrower: it focuses on memories from one specific season or theme, such as a single summer spent learning to sail.

qs.q: Why do journalists value firsthand accounts over rumors?
choices: Because rumors are always longer than a magazine profile.
Because someone present at the event can describe exact details.
Because eyewitnesses only write about joyful childhood summers.
Because firsthand accounts never need to follow chronological steps.
qs.why: Paragraph 4 explains that someone who stood on the scene can recount the exact steps detail by detail.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Writers choose among different nonfiction forms to fit each true story.
Autobiographies are always more accurate than shorter essays or profiles.
Coaches and grandmothers provide the best topics for every memoir.
Nonfiction writers should avoid sharing personal feelings in their books.
qs.why: Each paragraph introduces a different true-life form—from autobiography and memoir to anecdote, vignette, profile, and tribute—based on purpose and scope.

clues.text: pauses to think deeply about what those days meant
a brief true story told to make a point
a person who saw a big event with his own eyes
honors someone to show lasting thanks or care
